task.description:
Write the NEW regression test the design specifies in lib/letflow/design/iss0451-poller-crash-budget-isolation.md section 6 -- a new file test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker_test.exs. Read section 6 in full for the exact procedure/mechanism/observables (this is the authoritative spec; do not invent a different shape). Summary of what it must prove: a PERSISTENT Poller fault (the force_poller_crash flag is set and NEVER cleared during the test, unlike REQ-219's own AC4 test) causes Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers to repeatedly exhaust its own restart budget and get repeatedly restarted by PollersBreaker, which itself eventually trips to :open (per the design's stated consecutive-trip threshold) and stops trying -- and throughout all of this, Letflow.Supervisor (top-level), Letflow.Repo, and the Bandit listener (via Letflow.Supervisor.Http) all remain alive and untouched. This is WF-03's own required fail-then-pass proof per docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md's Steps 2-4 section: since PollersBreaker is a NEW module (not a fix to existing behavior), the fail-then-pass requirement is satisfied via MUTATION testing per that section's 'When the pre-fix failure is code under test does not exist' subsection -- you must mutate the shipped pollers_breaker.ex logic in specific, targeted ways (e.g. remove the trip-threshold check so it never opens; remove the :temporary child-spec change so the top-level auto-restarts again; break the backoff schedule) and record which of your new test's assertions fail for each mutant, in a throwaway git worktree or via revert-and-verify per that WF-03 section's own two techniques -- do not leave a mutated pollers_breaker.ex or application.ex in the tree at the end of this step.

Also write the design's stated new assertion for the EXISTING AC4 test if not already fully covered (check test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs's current AC4 test against design section 5 -- ELIXIR-DEV already updated it, confirm it matches the design's spec rather than assuming).
acceptance_criteria: test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker_test.exs created per design section 6's exact procedure/observables
The test proves Letflow.Supervisor/Letflow.Repo/Letflow.Supervisor.Http all survive a PERSISTENT (never-cleared) fault, not just a single crash event
At least 2 targeted mutants applied to pollers_breaker.ex/application.ex's shipped logic, each mutant's effect on the new test's assertions recorded (which fail, which still pass)
Mutation performed in a throwaway worktree OR reverted-and-verified with git status --porcelain empty and a clean re-run quoted in result.summary, per WF-03's own mutant-is-a-temporary-probe rule
No mutated file left in the tree at handoff completion

result.summary:
New test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker_test.exs written per design doc section 6 exactly: sets :force_poller_crash and NEVER clears it during the test body (the deliberate opposite of pollers_test.exs's own AC4 test), triggers the first Pollers exit via terminate_child+start_child, waits for PollersBreaker.breaker_state() to reach :open (up to 5s, actual: well under 1s), then asserts -- WHILE the fault is still active -- that Letflow.Repo/Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure/Letflow.Supervisor.Http/Letflow.Supervisor pids are all unchanged from before, that a Process.monitor on the top-level Supervisor never received a :DOWN, and that Process.whereis(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers) == nil (breaker genuinely holding it stopped, not restarted). Ran standalone: 'mix test test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker_test.exs' -> Result: 1 passed. Ran together with the existing AC4 test (both async: false, share the Pollers/PollersBreaker singletons): 'mix test test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_test.exs test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker_test.exs' -> Result: 5 passed, 0 failures -- no cross-file interference. 'mix compile --warnings-as-errors' clean, 0 warnings.

Verified ELIXIR-DEV's existing pollers_test.exs AC4 update against design section 5's revised 9-step procedure (rework iteration 3) line by line -- all 9 steps match exactly (single terminate_child trigger with no test-issued start_child call, wait_for_breaker_restart polling both pid-appears and breaker_state()==:closed, fault cleared immediately after, Repo/Infrastructure pid-unchanged assertions, new-pid assertions, the new breaker_state()==:closed confirming assertion, and the start_child/2-based restart_pollers!/0 teardown helper). No changes needed to that file.

Since Letflow.Supervisor.PollersBreaker is a brand-new module (not a fix to existing behavior), the fail-then-pass requirement was satisfied via mutation testing per WF-03's 'When the pre-fix failure is code under test does not exist' section, not a pre-fix-commit checkout (which would only prove UndefinedFunctionError, not discriminating power). Attempted the preferred throwaway-worktree technique first (git worktree add --detach), but the fresh worktree has no _build/deps (gitignored, would require mix deps.get with no guaranteed network access) -- fell back to the workflow doc's own second technique: mutate in place, revert with git checkout --, verify.

MUTANT 1 (lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker.ex, handle_pollers_down/1's 2nd-:DOWN-while-:closed clause): removed the trip-threshold check -- changed trip_to_open(state) to the same restart-and-rearm behavior as the 1st-:DOWN branch, so the breaker never opens no matter how many times Pollers re-exhausts. Ran 'mix test test/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker_test.exs' against the mutant -> Result: 0/1 passed -- failed exactly at 'assert wait_for_breaker_open(), \"PollersBreaker did not reach :open within the timeout\"' (5s timeout exhausted, breaker stuck :closed forever). Reverted: 'git checkout -- lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers_breaker.ex'. Verified: 'git status --porcelain' empty, re-ran the test -> Result: 1 passed.

MUTANT 2 (lib/letflow/application.ex children list): reverted 'Supervisor.child_spec(Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers, restart: :temporary)' back to a bare 'Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers' entry (implicit :permanent default), restoring the top-level auto-restart path the breaker design exists to eliminate. Ran the test against the mutant -> Result: 0/1 passed -- raised '** (CaseClauseError) no case clause matching: {:error, :already_present}' at the test's own trigger step (terminate_child then start_child), because a :permanent child's spec is not deleted by terminate_child/2 the way a :temporary child's is -- direct evidence the test (and PollersBreaker's identical restart_pollers/0) depends on the :temporary child-spec change specifically. Reverted: 'git checkout -- lib/letflow/application.ex'. Verified: 'git status --porcelain' empty, re-ran both files together -> Result: 5 passed, 0 failures.

Final state: git status --porcelain shows only the new test file and test/specs/ISS-0451.md (both intentional additions) -- no mutated lib/ file remains in the tree. Did not run the full 'mix letflow.check.test' suite per this handoff's own task instruction ('Do not run the FULL test suite -- this is a design/authoring step, not the run step') -- that instruction outranks the role file's default full-suite-gate step per core-directives.md's Instruction Precedence rule 1 (handoff task block is most specific); TEST-RUNNER runs the full suite next.
result.next_action: Route to TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR to independently verify coverage and re-apply at least one of the two reported mutants itself.
